text:
olga: quick sanity check — I'm about to land a tiny TF refactor that moves subnet AZ-affinity tags into the new network-sharding module and updates the TGW attachment to prefer the new subnets. plan looks fine but there are a couple of route propagation toggles that made me nervous. can someone scan?

olga: gist of the plan output i'm seeing:
```
# module.network.aws_subnet.this[2] will be updated in-place
~ resource "aws_subnet" "this" {
    tags = {
-     "az-affinity" = "3"
+     "az-shard"  = "3"
    }
  }

# aws_route_table_association.rta[1] will be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_route_table_association" "rta" {
+   ~ route_table_id = "rtb-aaa" -> "rtb-bbb"
  }

# aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_propagation.propagation: 
~ (forces replacement)
```

olga: the concern is a short window where the subnet is associated to a different RT and TGW propagation flips. last time we saw this it caused ephemeral SNAT failures for pod egress for ~20s during a canary.

ryan: can you paste the exact TF diff you plan to apply? small snippets are enough.

olga: sure, here's the relevant module change (only the part I touched):
```hcl
module "network-sharding" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra/modules/network-sharding.git//subnet"

  subnets = var.subnets
+  az_shard_tag_key = "az-shard"
-  az_affinity_tag_key = "az-affinity"
}

resource "aws_tgw_attachment" "redwood-apps" {
  transit_gateway_id = var.tgw_id
  subnet_ids        = module.network-sharding.subnet_ids_preferred
  # fallback uses the older subnet set if preferred not available
}
```

maya: two quick flags from past incidents:
- route_table_association replacement can cause brief egress blackholes if the instance/NAT mapping flips before TGW propagation completes. we mitigated before by doing the route swap in the same plan as the tgw propagation changes and adding explicit depends_on between rta and tgw_propagation.
- also add a short wait_for_propagation step in the deploy script (sleep + aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-tables to confirm).

zach: +1 to explicit depends_on. Also, do we have NATs in the same AZs you're re-tagging? if a subnet loses its previous RT before the natgw elastic ip moves, connections can be reset. recommend migrating a single AZ first (canary) and watching SNAT connections.

infra-bot: terraform plan completed. Summary: 3 to add, 2 to change, 1 to destroy. No data-sensitive output included.

devops-oncall: if you want to be safe, run this sequence:
1) pick one non-critical AZ (canary)
2) apply only subnet tag + create new subnet set (no route swaps)
3) attach TGW to new subnets (dont disable old attachment)
4) wait for propagation: run -> `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-tables --filters Name=transit-gateway-id,Values=${tgw}` and check propagated routes
5) flip route_table_association to point to new RTs in a single, short maintenance window (we can notify customers)
6) monitor `conntrack` and SNAT error rates in datadog (dash: network.egress.snat.errors)

olga: thanks all. plan update: i'll do a canary apply to az-shard=3 only, add depends_on between aws_route_table_association and aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_propagation, and include a 30s post-apply check that queries TGW route tables.

olga: example of the depends_on I'm adding:
```hcl
resource "aws_route_table_association" "rta" {
  subnet_id = aws_subnet.this[count.index].id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.main.id
  depends_on = [aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_propagation.propagation]
}
```

ryan: looks good. also consider adding `create_before_destroy = true` on the subnet module if the cloud account allows additional IPs.

maya: one more: add a short pager duty escalation if SNAT error rate > 5% for 2 minutes during canary.

olga: will do both. I'll post the canary plan output in this thread before applying. ETA ~30m. thanks! :thumbsup:

zach: ping me before you flip the routes and i'll watch the NAT metrics.

devops-oncall: i'll reserve a 10-min maintenance window on calendar id `infra-mgmt` starting in 45m.

olga: awesome — will follow up with a plan JSON and the exact apply command.

infra-bot: reminder: run `tfstate lock` if you need to prevent concurrent applies.

olga: noted, locking in place. will post results here.
